fix.notes: The JS only fires when the select value is empty, so it never overrides an archetype pre-selected by the rule engine. If a deck has no archetype assigned (archetype_id is 0 or null), jQuery's data() returns a falsy value and the guard `if (archetypeId && ...)` prevents any no-op selection.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

On `/admin/archetypes`, each queue row's "Assign To" dropdown defaulted to `[Select]` when no rule matched the deck, even though the deck already had a machine-guessed archetype assigned (e.g. via similarity matching). Admins had to manually locate the current archetype in the dropdown before they could confirm or change it.

## What changed

- **`decksite/templates/editarchetypes.mustache`**: Added `data-archetype-id="{{archetype_id}}"` to each `<tr>` in the queue, exposing the deck's current (machine-guessed) archetype ID as a data attribute.
- **`shared_web/static/js/pd.js`**: Added `PD.initArchetypeGuess()`, called from `PD.init()`, which on page load walks every queue row and sets its `<select>` to the deck's current archetype ID — but only when the select is still at its empty default (i.e. no rule already pre-selected a value).

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` passes (exit 0).
- No Python unit tests exist for this JS-only behaviour and no DB was available in the environment to run the full unit suite.

Fixes #12712
